title: The Articles of Confederation: America's First Constitution
learningObjectives: Describe the adoption of the Articles of Confederation on November 15, 1777 and its role as the first constitution until 1789.
Explain the committee drafting process, representation by state, and the requirement for unanimous ratification completed March 1, 1781.
Identify the weaknesses of the central government under the Articles that led to the Constitutional Convention in May 1787.

explanations.text: The Articles created a league of friendship with equal voting for each state and required all states to agree before the system could begin.

evidence.quote: This "first constitution of the United States" established a "league of friendship" for the 13 sovereign and independent states.
The Articles of Confederation also outlined a Congress with representation not based on population – each state would have one vote in Congress.

explanations.text: Limited central power to regulate commerce and collect revenue created crisis conditions that prompted a new convention to revise the system.

evidence.quote: With the states retaining considerable power, the central government had insufficient power to regulate commerce.
In May of 1787, the Constitutional Convention assembled in Philadelphia to revise the Articles of Confederation.

events.label: Congress appoints committees to plan confederation

evidence.quote: After the Lee Resolution proposed independence for the American colonies, the Second Continental Congress appointed three committees on June 11, 1776.
The Articles of Confederation were adopted by the Continental Congress on November 15, 1777.

events.label: Maryland ratifies and Confederation Congress begins

evidence.quote: When Maryland ratified it on March 1, 1781, the Congress of the Confederation came into being.
In May of 1787, the Constitutional Convention assembled in Philadelphia to revise the Articles of Confederation.
